title: Selection of Phage-displayed peptides that bind to cancer following treatment
protocol: Segregate and suspend monolayer cells with 80% confluence in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Develop heterotopic models by subcutaneously inoculating cell suspension (5x10^5 cells or adjusted for different cells) in nude mice.
Implant the tumors in both hind limbs of mice and use for experiments when the tumor size reaches 0.5 cm in diameter.
Administer phage libraries intracardiac injection at 4 hours following irradiation after treating the tumor-bearing mice.
Euthanize the mice after 10 minutes of circulation and perfuse with 10 ml of PBS into the left ventricle that were recovered from the right atrium.
Perfuse with PBS at a rate of 2 ml per minute to remove phages that stayed in circulation but did not bind to blood vessels.
Sacrifice mice to remove organs and tumors for quantifying plaque-forming units.
Weigh the organs so that the number of phage can be normalized by weight of the organ.
Disrupt the tissues using a hand-held homogenizer on ice.
Clean the homogenizer with bleach and rinse with PBS between homogenization of different organs.
Microcentrifuge the homogenate at 5000 rpm and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellets and wash 5 times with PBS.
Amplify T7 phages bound to tumors by adding E. coli BL21 into the washed pellets.
Titrate the resuspended cell pellets in bacterial culture in 15 minutes when the phage infection has occurred but amplification is not yet complete.
Normalize the titers of phages recovered from each tissue with the weight of each tissue.
Amplify the phages recovered from the treated tumors at 37°C with shaking until the culture is lysed (in around 2.5 hours).
Centrifuge the cultures at 8000 rpm for 15 minutes to have the amplified phages in supernatants.
Partially purify the amplified phages by PEG-precipitation and resuspend in PBS for next round of biopanning.
Repeat these steps after six rounds of biopanning.
Isolate single plaques from soft agar.
Amplify gene fragments encoding peptides polymerase chain reaction (PCR) following standard protocols.
Treat or inject tumor-bearing mice with 1×10^9 pfu of HVGGSSV phage or control phage, respectively.
Remove and fix the tumors at 48 hours after administration of phages.
Stain phages in tumor tissue with anti-T7 phage polyclonal antibodies.
Use a secondary IgG-HRP conjugate to visualize primary antibody binding by using DAB as substrate for HRP.
Counterstain tissues with Hematoxylin.
Perform TUNEL staining.
Label PEG-precipitated phages, synthetic HVGGSSV peptide, or streptavidin with amine-reactive Cy7 dye following the manufacturer's instructions.
Inject labeled phages or the complex of biotinylated peptide and streptavidin-Cy7 conjugate into the circulation via tail vein or jugular vein catheter in tumor-bearing mice.
Take near infrared images with IVIS imaging system at various time points after injection.
Measure radiance (photons/sec/cm²) in the region of interest by using the program provided by Xenogen.
Normalize radiance from peptide within tumors to that of the whole body while correlating peptide binding (radiance) to tumor response (tumor growth).
Implant tumors in hind limbs of mice.
Start treatment when tumor size reaches 0.5 cm in diameter with groups including irradiation (IR, 3 Gy), SU11248 (40 mg/kg), combined treatment with IR and SU11248, and untreated control.
Administer SU11248 through intraperitoneal injection once a day for 5 consecutive days.
Measure tumor size every other day using calipers to calculate fold increase in tumor volume compared to the first day of treatment.
Include six animals in each group.
